name: Full Range
opportunity: Nike's basketball shorts ladder is priced upside-down: the shortest inseam costs the most and the longest, most size-inclusive product costs the least. Verified 2 Sep 2026: Nike DNA 6" lists at USD 65 (nike.com/t/dna-mens-dri-fit-6-basketball-shorts-R65pLfb2, 2026-09-02) while the DNA Academy 11" - the coverage length, and the style Kohl's carries in Big & Tall through 3XL/4XL and 4XL Tall - lists at USD 37 (kohls.com/product/prd-7499374, 2026-09-02), with the DNA 10" at USD 50 discounting to about USD 30.97 (A02-S4). Nike therefore prices coverage and extended sizes as cheapness for the three groups that most need them: coverage-first and modest-dressing players (A05-S8), plus/big-and-tall players who default to AND1 at USD 9.98 to 5XL (A01-S9), and the long-inseam retro buyer for whom 9 inches or more is the defining spec (A05-S3). The opportunity is to build a properly constructed long tier - heavier mesh, real waist control on hip-first grading (A06-S9), women's-graded coverage lengths, extended sizes offered at the TOP of the range rather than only at the bottom - and sell it at USD 55 on the performance wall in wholesale doors that are growing (A02-S7).
target_consumer:
Three groups currently served by the same USD 37 SKU, by Nike's cheapest franchises in extended sizes, or by value and licensed-heritage brands.

(1) COVERAGE-FIRST WOMEN AND GIRLS, 16-35: taller and longer-legged players (the Griner-type body: 'I got a lot of leg. I need to cover it up a little bit' - A05-S8, quote dated May 2014, see contradictions) and modest-dressing athletes, including Muslim players in the US, UK, Southeast Asia and Africa, who need a real 9-inch women's-block length in every size rather than a tall-size workaround (A03-S6, A06-S9). Note: France bans the hijab in federated play, so France is a non-market for the modest use case (A05-S8).

(2) PLUS, TALL AND BIG-AND-TALL MEN, 18-45: the buyer visible in the value channel choosing AND1 'All Court' 11-inch up to 5XL at USD 9.98 (walmart.com/ip/5113233336, verified 2026-09-02), described by one reviewer as 'affordable and cultural' versus Nike or adidas (A01-S9), or buying Mitchell & Ness Swingman in Big & Tall at DXL (A02-S5). Inside Nike this consumer already exists but is met almost entirely by the two cheapest franchises: Kohl's Big & Tall Nike basketball assortment is DNA Academy 11" at USD 37 and Dri-FIT Icon (kohls.com, 2026-09-02).

(3) THE LONG-INSEAM LIFESTYLE AND RETRO BUYER, 16-30: for whom 9 inches or longer is the spec that defines the look (Hibbett's own guidance: retro leans 9"+, modern 7" or shorter - A05-S3), who currently buys Mitchell & Ness or a Nike short whose price signals 'entry'.

All three buy predominantly in wholesale and extended-size doors - Dick's, Kohl's, Academy, Hibbett, JD, Amazon, DXL - the channel that grew 4% at Nike in FY26 while Nike Digital fell for a tenth straight quarter (A02-S7).
consumer_problem_jtbd:
"Give me a basketball short that actually covers me and actually fits me - in my length and my size - without the product telling me I bought the cheap one."

The job has three layers. FUNCTIONAL: a length that clears the knee in a defensive stance and stays put through roughly 450 lateral movements and 42-56 jumps a game (A06-S1); a waist that holds when the garment is graded hip-first, because Nike's own guidance tells women whose waist and hip fall in different sizes to 'order according to your hip measurement', which loads all the slack onto a drawcord (A06-S9); fabric that does not go sheer or lose its shape - the Icon franchise draws 'paper-thin', see-through, holes-in-seams-after-one-wash complaints and shows 3.9 stars with 67% recommending across 64 reviews at Dick's (A04-S6), and Nike shorts sizing is reported four different ways on the same SKU (A01-S2).

EMOTIONAL / SOCIAL: coverage is currently priced as a discount. A player who needs 11 inches or a 3XL is routed to Nike's cheapest make, while the 6-inch buyer is sold a USD 65 short. The consumer reads the ladder correctly.

ECONOMIC: the value alternative is genuinely cheap and genuinely inclusive - AND1 at USD 9.98 to 5XL - so the job is not 'be cheaper', it is 'be worth USD 55 in a length and size that has never had a USD 55 option'.
product_idea:
NIKE BASKETBALL FULL RANGE - a long-length, fully-graded tier built on the DNA franchise chassis and merchandised on the performance wall, not in the value bin. Naming direction: 'DNA Full Range' as the SKU name, 'Full Range' as the architecture name that also carries the size story; the existing DNA Academy 11" stays in the line at USD 37 as the opening price point so the ladder gains a step instead of losing one.

SILHOUETTE: straight-leg performance basketball short, moderate leg opening, sitting at or just above the knee on the body it is graded for. Deliberately not a jort and not a tapered 5-inch: this is the hoops length built properly. Two blocks share one graphic and fabric system.

INSEAMS: Men's/unisex 9" and 11". Women's 7" and 9", with the 9" carried in EVERY size and colour rather than existing only as a tall-size derivative (A03-S6 notes tall sizes run 2" longer; that is a workaround, not a length offer). A separate +1.5" TALL length grade on the same nominal waist for both blocks, so 'tall' means longer legs, not a bigger waist. NOTE: the 6-vs-11 inseam argument is NOT resolved by this brief and is not resolved by the evidence base (A07-S4 argues the poles, A02-S5's own cited source says 7-9", Nike's live ladder runs 6-11" continuously). Full Range is a bet that the long end deserves construction and price, not a bet that the short end is wrong.

SIZE RUN: Men's S-4XL plus S Tall-4XL Tall. Women's XS-3X. Extended sizes carried in every colourway and both lengths, at the same MSRP - no size upcharge, no extended-size-only cheaper make. This is the load-bearing decision: today Nike's Big & Tall basketball offer at Kohl's is the DNA Academy 11" and the Icon - its two cheapest franchises (verified 2026-09-02).

FABRIC: heavier-gauge double-knit basketball mesh - open-hole outer face, smooth knit inner face (the construction Nike's own DNA copy already describes) - targeted materially heavier than the current value-long make so it hangs rather than clings, is not see-through at extended sizes, and holds shape through wash. Target spec, to be set against Nike's own GSM history: a published minimum wash-cycle dimensional-stability and seam-strength claim on the hangtag, because the reproducible complaint on the cheap long franchises is seam failure and shrinkage after one wash, not pockets (A01-S3, A04-S6). Recycled content stays a compliance baseline, not a lead claim, and any EU claim language must clear the EU Empowering Consumers Directive applying from 27 Sep 2026 (A03-S5).

WAIST - THE ENGINEERING CONTENT: 45-50mm non-roll waistband; internal two-point adjustable elastic draw tape in addition to the external flat cord, so the waist is controlled by structure rather than by a cord that slips when saturated (A06-S9, A06-T6); silicone tape inside the back waistband; back rise lifted ~1.5-2cm on the women's block and on the extended men's grades to stop gapping in a low stance. Inseam printed on the size label and on the PDP, because the same Nike short is currently reported as running big, small, true and long (A01-S2).

CONSTRUCTION: gusseted crotch and articulated side seams tested in a defensive lateral stance, not standing (A06-S1). Linerless as standard on both long lengths with a lined option, rather than assuming layering behaviour that the evidence does not establish (A06-S6 is weak).

STORAGE: dual side pockets plus one bonded, bartacked zip utility pocket at the right hip seam sized for a 6.7-inch phone, with anchored pocket bags. Plus a POCKETLESS, clean-panel 9" competition variant for team and roster use, since FIBA requires shorts to end above the knee with colour-matched compression and NFHS Rule 3-4-5 now permits multiple styles of like-coloured uniform bottoms among teammates (A06-S3) - a rules opening that makes a graded long bottom legal in US high-school play for the first time.

COLOURWAYS: a replenishable core carried year-round in every size and both lengths - black, white, university red, royal, midnight navy, dark grey heather - plus two seasonal colour injections. Surface interest comes from a tonal jacquard waistband and hem trim rather than from graphics; the retro striped-waistband code is saturated from USD 15 to USD 150 and is not a differentiator (A07-S6, A07-S9). Differentiation here is construction, grading and price, deliberately not print.
why_now:
Four clocks are running at once.

1. THE INVERSION IS LIVE AND CHECKABLE TODAY. Nike DNA 6" USD 65 versus DNA Academy 11" USD 37 including Big & Tall to 4XL Tall, with the 10" discounting roughly 38% (A02-S4; verified 2026-09-02 at nike.com and kohls.com). Every quarter it stands, it trains the coverage buyer that Nike's answer for them is the cheap one.

2. THE VALUE FLOOR IS RISING FOR THE FIRST TIME IN A DECADE. US de minimis for China/HK ended 2 May 2025 and apparel now carries roughly a 53.5% combined duty stack; Temu and Shein US audiences remain about 30% below pre-tariff baseline as of April 2026 (A02-S4 counter-evidence). The value and licensed-heritage brands holding this length - AND1, Amazon private label, Mitchell & Ness - are the ones most exposed. The window to enter above them narrows as they reprice.

3. THE CHANNEL HAS SWUNG TO WHOLESALE. Nike wholesale grew 4% in Q4 and full-year FY26 while Nike Digital fell for a tenth consecutive quarter, down 12% in the quarter (A02-S7); Nike's Performance business grew mid-single digits led by Running, Football and Basketball while Sportswear and Jordan streetwear stayed challenged (A04-S1). Extended-size and long-inseam volume lives almost entirely in wholesale and extended-size doors - Kohl's, Dick's, Academy, Hibbett, Amazon, DXL - which is exactly where Nike is currently winning.

4. UNITS ARE FLAT, SO MIX IS THE ONLY LEVER. Nike Brand apparel grew to USD 13.4B in FY26 on units +1% with ASP contributing about 1 point, and that ASP came from mix, partially offset by higher discounts (A03-S9). Moving long-inseam and extended-size units from USD 37 to USD 55 is a mix move that does not require category growth, a new consumer, or a price increase above the USD 100 line Nike froze in June 2025 (A04-S8).

Counter-clock, stated honestly: the US marketplace turned 'increasingly promotional' in summer 2026 and Foot Locker comps fell 3.6% (A04-S4) - though Ed Stack attributed that to footwear and retro exposure at one banner while the Dick's banner comped +4.9%.

key_features_benefits.feature: Coverage lengths priced as product, not as entry: 9" and 11" men's and 7"/9" women's at a single USD 55 MSRP, with the existing DNA Academy 11" held at USD 37 beneath it
key_features_benefits.benefit: Breaks the ladder inversion in one move. The consumer who needs length stops being routed to the cheapest make, and Nike gains a step in the ladder instead of losing one. ASP-accretive mix in a flat-unit environment.

key_features_benefits.feature: Extended sizes at the TOP of the range: men's S-4XL plus Tall grades and women's XS-3X, carried in every colourway and both lengths at the same price, with no extended-size-only cheaper make
key_features_benefits.benefit: Removes the size upcharge and the size downgrade at once. Directly addresses the plus and big-and-tall player currently choosing AND1 to 5XL on price and inclusion, and the woman who cannot get her length above XL today.

key_features_benefits.feature: Structural waist control on hip-first grading: 45-50mm non-roll band, internal two-point adjustable elastic in addition to the external cord, silicone tape at the back, back rise lifted 1.5-2cm on women's and extended grades
key_features_benefits.benefit: Fixes the mechanical consequence of sizing by hip - slack that a drawcord alone cannot hold, and that slips when saturated. The single most defensible construction difference between this and a value long short.

key_features_benefits.feature: Heavier double-knit mesh with a published wash-cycle dimensional-stability and seam-strength spec on the hangtag
key_features_benefits.benefit: Answers the reproducible complaint on Nike's cheap long franchises - seams failing and shrinkage after one wash, 'paper-thin' and see-through - which is what would otherwise kill a USD 55 ask at the long end. Not-see-through matters disproportionately at extended sizes.

key_features_benefits.feature: Inseam and grade printed on the label and PDP; one consistent block across lengths and sizes
key_features_benefits.benefit: Cuts the online return risk on a product bought overwhelmingly in wholesale and marketplace doors, where the same Nike short is currently reported as running big, small, true and long simultaneously.

key_features_benefits.feature: A pocketless clean-panel 9" competition variant alongside the pocketed retail version
key_features_benefits.benefit: Makes the same block legal for FIBA and US high-school play. NFHS Rule 3-4-5 now permits multiple styles of like-coloured uniform bottoms among teammates, explicitly to allow religious and personal accommodation without a permission request - a rules change that legalises a graded long bottom on the same roster.

key_features_benefits.feature: Replenishable six-colour core carried year-round in every size and length, bought for reorder rather than for markdown, in wholesale and extended-size doors
key_features_benefits.benefit: Matches where the volume actually moved - wholesale +4% while Nike Digital fell for a tenth straight quarter - and protects full price in a category where the 10" already discounts about 38% and Mitchell & Ness clears from USD 79.99 to USD 35.99.

key_features_benefits.feature: Construction and grading as the differentiator, not retro graphics; tonal jacquard waistband and hem trim only
key_features_benefits.benefit: Avoids the saturated vintage-hoops code that runs from USD 15 TikTok Shop listings to USD 150 collabs, and avoids competing with Mitchell & Ness on licence, where Nike cannot win on team IP in fan doors.

target_price.tier: Mid / core-performance - one step above Nike's current long-inseam opening price point (DNA Academy 11" at USD 37), one step below the DNA 6" at USD 65, and inside the sub-USD 100 band, so no premium-tier claim is required to make it work
target_price.rationale:
Anchors, all either verified this session or carried from the evidence base. Nike's own ladder: DNA 6" USD 65 (nike.com, verified 2026-09-02); Standard Issue 8" USD 55; DNA 10" USD 50 discounting to about USD 30.97; DNA Academy 11" USD 37 including Big & Tall through 4XL Tall (kohls.com, verified 2026-09-02) - a USD 37-65 span with the longest length at the lowest price (A02-S4, A02-S5). Competitors: AND1 All Court 11" up to 5XL at USD 9.98 (walmart.com, verified 2026-09-02); Amazon Essentials 2-pack USD 7.97; adidas' 2025 hero Crazy Lite short from USD 50 (A07-S9 domain evidence); New Balance 7" mesh USD 50, selling USD 37.50 at Foot Locker (A02-S4); Mitchell & Ness Swingman USD 79.99 list, clearing USD 35.99 (A02-S4 counter-evidence); Nike Sabrina women's short USD 65 (A03-S6).

USD 55 is chosen because: (a) it sits at the existing Standard Issue 8" rung, so it is a length extension of a price Nike already holds rather than a new price; (b) it is USD 18 above the current 11" and therefore a real trade-up rather than a re-sticker; (c) it stays under USD 100, where Nike's June 2025 action left prices unchanged - meaning this must be engineered to margin at USD 55, not rescued by a price increase, against roughly USD 1.5B of annualised tariff cost and a 120bp FY26 gross-margin headwind (A04-S8); (d) it is 5.5x the AND1 alternative, which is the number the consumer-research plan has to defeat, and the honest reason the confidence score is not higher.

The extended-size no-upcharge rule is a deliberate margin choice: extended sizes consume more fabric, so a flat MSRP costs points. That cost is the mechanism of the idea and should be carried as a stated investment, not engineered away by making the big sizes cheaper - which is precisely the behaviour being corrected.
target_price.regional_notes:
Lead markets US, then UK/EU and Australia. Indicative: EUR 54.99 / GBP 47.99 / AUD 85. Any EU recycled-content or sustainability language must clear the EU Empowering Consumers Directive applying from 27 September 2026, which bans generic and uncertified environmental claims (A03-S5).

Australia is an attractive secondary: about 1.3 million players, second among team sports, female participation up 25% since 2022 to more than 450,000 women and girls, NBL 2025-26 attendance 1,231,796 (+9%), and the league's on-court partner is Champion rather than a performance-basketball leader (A02-S9 domain evidence, carried in A02-S7's channel logic).

Greater China is deliberately NOT a lead market for this opportunity and this should be said out loud, because the brief's Worldball priority pulls the other way: Nike GC revenue fell 13% currency-neutral in FY26 with apparel units down 8%, Li-Ning basketball retail fell 19%, and the branded basketball segment there is promotional for everyone (A02-S7 channel context, A04-S1). A price-and-size architecture move needs a market where Nike's wholesale shelf is healthy. Philippines and SEA pricing (roughly PHP 3,000 at this MSRP) is likely above the local value band and should be tested, not assumed.

market_distribution_role:
ROLE IN LINE: a franchise extension and a replenishable core, not a hero and not a drop. Full Range is the long-and-extended tier of DNA - the rung that currently does not exist between the USD 37 opening 11" and the USD 65 6". It should be planned as carry-over with two seasonal colour injections, bought for reorder against sell-through rather than for a seasonal markdown cycle, because the 10" already discounts about 38% and the heritage tier it competes against clears from USD 79.99 to USD 35.99 (A02-S4).

CHANNEL MIX: wholesale-led, roughly 70/30 wholesale to Nike Direct at launch, inverting Nike's usual instinct. Nike wholesale grew 4% in both Q4 and full-year FY26 while Nike Digital declined for a tenth consecutive quarter (A02-S7), and extended-size and long-inseam volume is concentrated in the doors that merchandise size: Kohl's (which already carries Nike Big & Tall basketball shorts through 4XL Tall), Dick's, Academy, Hibbett, JD, Amazon (where Nike has sold directly since July 2025), and big-and-tall specialty such as DXL, where Mitchell & Ness already sells Swingman shorts in Big & Tall. Nike.com's role is the extended-size and length long tail - it already runs both a Women's Plus Size Basketball Shorts and a Men's Big & Tall Basketball Shorts category page (nike.com, verified 2026-09-02) - which is where the full size run can be held without door-level inventory risk.

SECOND CHANNEL, LOW COST TO TEST: the team-dealer route. NFHS Rule 3-4-5 now permits multiple styles of like-coloured uniform bottoms on the same roster (A06-S3), which makes a graded long bottom orderable through dealers alongside a standard game short. Bookings-led team business is low-markdown and grows with participation rather than with mall traffic (A04-S5 context on the women's demand call-out at Dick's and Foot Locker). Treat as a pilot, not a plan - the dealer channel is consolidating under a KKR-backed buyer and Nike's competitive position there is unmeasured.

LEAD MARKETS: US first (where the inversion, the value competitor and the big-and-tall channel all sit), then UK/EU and Australia. Greater China explicitly deprioritised for this opportunity.

LAUNCH CADENCE: SS28 as a full-year core drop with a Holiday 27 wholesale sell-in, so the buy is set against reorder data rather than a single season. Two colour injections a season. Deliberately no collab, no drop mechanic, no athlete story at launch - the proposition is that the product is better made and correctly priced, and an athlete story would let the buy be judged on heat instead of on sell-through. One SS28 timing note the base surfaced elsewhere and should be checked against the buy: LA28 opens in July 2028, inside the SS28 selling season, in Nike's home market.

evidence_stack.contribution: Supplies the decisive datapoint and the channel. A02-S4's own skeptic counter-evidence establishes Nike's live ladder as DNA 6" USD 65 / Standard Issue 8" USD 55 / DNA 10" USD 50 marked to USD 30.97 / DNA Academy 11" USD 37 including Big & Tall - the inversion. A02-S5's counter-evidence adds that Nike's live men's range is 6-11 inches, not the 6/8/10 the specialist described, and that the 11" is stocked at Nike.com, Dick's, Academy, Kohl's and Amazon, plus the Mitchell & Ness benchmark at USD 79.99 list / USD 35.99 clearing. A02-S7 establishes that wholesale (+4% in Q4 and FY26) is where this product must sell, against Nike Digital's tenth straight quarterly decline. Note the irony the synthesis flagged: the inversion appears in this base only as skeptic counter-evidence used to REFUTE other recommendations, never as a finding in its own right.

A01-S9 identifies the plus and big-and-tall value buyer - AND1 'up to 5XL' called 'affordable and cultural' versus Nike or adidas, and multipack replenishment behaviour in youth. A01-S2 and A01-S3 supply the two failure modes a USD 55 long short must not repeat: unpredictable grading (the same Jordan short reported as running big, small, true and long) and, per the skeptic's own retrieval of the Walmart Icon corpus, seam failure and post-wash shrinkage rather than pocket failure. All three are weakly evidenced: A01-S9 rests on unranked marketplace listings and a single anonymous review, A01-S2 is base-rate neglect without a returns benchmark, and A01-S3's failure half did not reproduce.

A05-S8 is the coverage-first need - taller and longer-legged women players and modest-dressing athletes for whom the short-shorts wave does not work - and it is explicitly a HYPOTHESIS, not a fact. A05-S3 supplies the usable spec split from Hibbett's own page: retro runs 9 inches or longer, modern 7 inches or shorter, which is the concrete definition of the length this tier occupies. A05-S9 corroborates that wide-cut and longer silhouettes are live in 2026 while simultaneously showing micro shorts are too - the churn is the finding.

A06-S9 supplies the construction thesis: Nike's own guidance tells women whose waist and hip fall in different sizes to order by hip, which loads the waist onto a drawcord - the mechanical reason a long women's short needs structural waist control. A06-S1 is the only untouched signal in its set and sets the fit-test protocol: up to 450 lateral movements and 42-56 jumps per game means fit is validated in a defensive stance, not standing. A06-S3 supplies the rules opening: NFHS Rule 3-4-5 (2025-26) now permits multiple styles of like-coloured uniform bottoms among teammates, explicitly for religious and personal accommodation - the newest and most actionable constraint change in the entire base, and the one that makes a graded long bottom legal on a US high-school roster.

A03-S6 proves women will pay USD 65 for genuine women's construction (Sabrina: woven front, knit back, snap cargo, plus-size SKU FB8427) and exposes the exact defect this brief fixes - length choice offered via tall sizing rather than as a length, and a reversible with pockets on only one side. A03-S9 is the commercial frame, verified from Nike's FY2026 filing: apparel USD 13.4B, units +1%, ASP contributing about 1 point from mix and already eroded by discounting - so a mix move is the available lever. A03-S5 sets the EmpCo compliance date of 27 September 2026 on any EU sustainability claim.

A04-S8 is the margin constraint and, read against the value competitor, the tailwind: Nike's June 2025 US action left everything under USD 100 unchanged, so the whole shorts ladder absorbed cost inflation, while its counter-evidence puts Nike's tariff exposure at USD 1.5B with a 120bp gross-margin headwind. The same duty stack is repricing the USD 4-10 value floor this idea sits above. A04-S6 supplies the quality evidence that a USD 55 long short must answer - Icon at 3.9 stars and 67% recommending across 64 reviews at Dick's. A04-S4 is the promotional risk. A04-S1 confirms Performance basketball is growing while Sportswear and Jordan streetwear are challenged, though its skeptic correctly notes that growth is footwear-weighted.

A07-S4 is included here as the OPPOSING design position, deliberately preserved: it argues Nike should design at the poles and abandon the 9-10 inch middle. Its counter-evidence is what makes it useful - Nike DNA ships a continuous 6/8/10 ladder with pockets at every length, and the Foot Locker '5 Inch Basketball Shorts' page that anchors the argument is an auto-generated attribute facet, not a merchandising bet. A07-S6 and A07-S9 supply the graphic discipline: women's shorts are under-designed as objects while retro codes are saturated from USD 15 to USD 150, so differentiation should sit in construction and grading rather than in print.

contradictory_evidence.description: THE INSEAM DIRECTION IS UNRESOLVED AND SITS DIRECTLY UNDER THIS IDEA. A07-S4 says proportion has split to the poles and Nike should abandon the 9-10 inch middle. A02-S5's own cited source (Under Armour Playbook) says modern performance shorts run 7-9 inches and Curry wears 7-9, contradicting its own headline. A05-S3's Hibbett source says retro runs 9 inches or longer. Nike's live ladder runs 6-11 inches continuously with pockets at every length, and 2026 fashion coverage names baggy AND micro shorts as simultaneous top trends. The cross-dataset auditor's verdict is that nobody in this base holds a single unit of sell-through evidence about which way basketball shorts specifically are moving, and that the churn itself is the finding. Full Range is a bet on the long end being under-built, NOT a bet that the long end is growing. If unit share by inseam shows 8-10 inch collapsing, this becomes a smaller, size-only opportunity rather than a length-and-size one.

EVERY PRICE IN THIS BRIEF SITS ON AN UNVERIFIED LADDER. The auditor found three mutually incompatible Nike price ladders in the base, none of them from a retrieved page, and warned that some figures may be search engines echoing query language back. I independently reproduced three anchors this session (DNA 6" USD 65, DNA Academy 11" USD 37 including Big & Tall at Kohl's, AND1 11" to 5XL USD 9.98), but every retail host - nike.com, kohls.com, dxl.com - was blocked to WebFetch, so these remain search-result summaries rather than retrieved pages. Nike's internal list-versus-realised ASP and markdown rate by inseam is the only thing that settles the USD 55 position.

THE COVERAGE-FIRST NEED IS A DECADE STALE AND ITS WHITESPACE CLAIM IS CONTRADICTED. The Griner 'I got a lot of leg' quote traces to a May 2014 Mother Jones interview, not 2018; the Minnesota Muslim girls' uniform project is the Asiya work of 2015-2017; Asiya has sold modest basketball components for roughly a decade. And Nike already markets an 11-inch short explicitly for 'extra coverage' and already sells a 9-inch women's short. This session confirmed Nike runs live 'Womens Plus Size Basketball Shorts' and 'Mens Big & Tall Basketball Shorts' category pages. So the whitespace is NOT that coverage and extended sizes are absent from Nike's line - it is that they are priced and constructed as the entry make. That is a narrower and less certain claim than the synthesis implies, and it must be argued against Nike's shipped assortment rather than against an imagined absence. France separately bans the hijab in federated play, so it is a non-market for the modest use case.

THE PLUS-SIZE AND VALUE BEHAVIOUR HAS NO POS DATA BEHIND IT. 'Amazon best-seller listings are dominated by multipacks' is a search-results impression treated as market data, with no best-seller rank, unit figure or date. The AND1 'affordable and cultural' quote is one anonymous review on one retailer. And the counter-evidence cuts the other way: value-channel Nike buyers also post strongly positive reviews ('very good quality', 'favorite shorts to wear'), so the extended-size value buyer is not demonstrably a Nike-rejecting segment. The AND1 buyer at USD 9.98 may be a pure price buyer who will not trade to USD 55 at any construction level - which is the single most likely way this opportunity fails.

THE WAIST-CONTROL THESIS RESTS ON SIZING BOILERPLATE. 'Order according to your hip measurement' is Nike's generic women's-bottoms guidance, appearing identically on the Women's Bottoms and Women's Numeric charts, and is standard industry practice - not a basketball-specific fit statement. The signal's own author conceded 'I found no independent quantitative data on women's basketball shorts fit complaints; this is a gap.' The inference from that sentence to 'the waist is systematically under-fitted, therefore build an internal adjustable band' has no evidence at any link. Waist gap may not be the actual complaint; hem length or taper may be.

IS THE SUB-USD 100 LADDER FROZEN OR NOT? The margin case for engineering to USD 55 rather than pricing up assumes the June 2025 exemption of everything under USD 100 still stands. The auditor verified that it has been superseded: Nike's tariff exposure rose from about USD 1B to USD 1.5B, the FY26 gross-margin headwind from about 75bp to 120bp, and Nike has continued taking surgical increases - apparel up about 3% - while facing a proposed US class action over tariff pricing. Whether USD 55 is a stretch or already conservative depends on the actual FY27 price file, which nobody in this base has seen.

THE PROMOTIONAL FLOOR IS BOTH REAL AND OVERSTATED, AND IT IS WORST EXACTLY HERE. Ed Stack's 'increasingly promotional' quote is real, but he attributed the damage to Foot Locker's exposure to legacy footwear silhouettes and retro product while the Dick's banner comped +4.9%, and Foot Locker US comps were +6% in Q1 2026 before -3.6% in Q2. Against that: the long tier is precisely where discounting already runs - Nike's own 10" at about 38% off, Mitchell & Ness clearing from USD 79.99 to USD 35.99, New Balance USD 50 selling at USD 37.50. A new USD 55 rung entering a length band that is already the most promoted band in the category is the commercial risk this brief cannot resolve from public data.

THE USD 65 WOMEN'S WILLINGNESS-TO-PAY MAY BE LIFESTYLE, NOT PERFORMANCE. Sabrina reviewers report wearing the shorts at home more often than playing basketball, because they are lightweight and comfortable, and describe them as versatile and gender-neutral. If the USD 65 Sabrina price proves lifestyle comfort demand rather than demand for women-specific court construction, then the read-across to a USD 55 women's coverage short built on grading and waist structure is weaker than it appears - and the winning feature set might be softness and drape rather than waistband engineering.

'BASKETBALL IS GROWING' IS A FOOTWEAR STATEMENT. Nike's FY26 Performance growth led by Running, Football and Basketball is real, but Nike discloses no basketball apparel line and the externally visible basketball momentum is signature-footwear-weighted, with Kobe alone at roughly 37% of signature basketball shoe sales on StockX in 2025. The category tailwind cited for this investment does not demonstrably extend to shorts, and the CFO said sell-through continues to struggle with marketplace conditions unlikely to improve through at least H1 FY2027.

confidence_rationale:
58 reflects an unusually asymmetric evidence profile: the STRUCTURAL observation is close to verified while the DEMAND response is close to unevidenced.

What pushes it up. The inversion itself is the best-supported claim in this brief and I reproduced it independently this session against three separate hosts: Nike DNA 6" at USD 65, DNA Academy 11" at USD 37 carried in Big & Tall through 3XL/4XL/4XL Tall at Kohl's, and the value alternative AND1 All Court 11" to 5XL at USD 9.98 (all 2026-09-02). The Big & Tall assortment at Kohl's being composed of exactly Nike's two cheapest franchises - DNA Academy and Icon - is a direct confirmation of the 'extended sizes only at the bottom' claim rather than an inference from it. The channel logic is verified (A02-S7), the commercial frame is verified from Nike's FY2026 filing (A03-S9), the rules opening is verified and dated (A06-S3), and the fix is a line-architecture and construction change rather than a technology bet - low innovation risk, short development path, no dependency on an unproven platform.

What holds it down, and these are not small. (1) There is no unit share by inseam anywhere in this base, so nobody can say whether the long end is a growing pool or a shrinking one - the auditor's explicit verdict. (2) Every demand-side signal underneath the idea is weak: the coverage-first need is a HYPOTHESIS built on 2014-2017 sources (A05-S8), the plus-size behaviour is unranked marketplace listings and one anonymous review (A01-S9), and the waist-control need is deduced from generic sizing boilerplate (A06-S9). (3) Willingness to pay is completely untested. The gap from USD 9.98 to USD 55 is 5.5x, and the gap from Nike's own USD 37 to USD 55 is a 49% trade-up asked of the single most price-sensitive buyer in the category. (4) The whitespace is narrower than the synthesis framing: Nike already runs women's plus-size and men's big-and-tall basketball shorts pages, so this is a repricing-and-reconstruction move inside a live assortment, not an entry into empty space. (5) The long tier is already the most discounted band in the category.

58 is where a PLM should take it to Consumer Council as a fundable hypothesis with two cheap, decisive tests attached - not as a signed-off brief.
what_would_need_to_be_true: The 9-11 inch band must still be a material share of Nike basketball shorts units. Unit share by inseam for the last 6-8 quarters, from Nike DTC plus at least two wholesale partners, split men's/women's and performance versus lifestyle door, by region. If 8-10 inch units are collapsing, this is a size opportunity only and the length half must be cut.

Extended sizes must actually be concentrated in Nike's cheapest makes. Pull the internal price file and size-curve fill for basketball shorts by inseam AND by size, showing what MSRP is available at 2X/3X/4X and at women's 1X-3X. The Kohl's Big & Tall assortment (DNA Academy 11" and Icon) is consistent with the claim but is one retailer at one snapshot.

The extended-size and long-inseam buyer must trade up. A willingness-to-pay test - conjoint or a live price test in one wholesale door - on a USD 37-to-USD 55 step for a heavier, better-graded long short, run separately for the AND1 buyer at USD 9.98 and the Nike USD 37 buyer, because they may not be the same person.

The quality gap must be real and fixable. Fabric GSM history for DNA Academy and Icon FY23-FY26, plus a 20-wash shrinkage, opacity and seam-strength test against AND1, Russell and Mitchell & Ness. If GSM was never reduced and the complaints are fit or expectation, the construction investment is aimed at the wrong defect.

Waist gap must be the actual women's complaint. A fit study on 100+ female players aged 14-30 across two markets, capturing waist-to-hip drop against current grading, plus a structured returns taxonomy coded for waist gap, hem length, ride-up and pocket. If hem length or taper dominates, redirect the engineering.

USD 55 must clear margin. Landed cost and gross margin by SKU with tariff exposure by sourcing country, modelled with the extended-size fabric consumption at a flat MSRP, and read against the current FY27 US price file - not the June 2025 exemption, which has been superseded by roughly 3% apparel increases.

Wholesale buyers must give it the door space. Confirmed size-run commitments from Kohl's, Dick's, Academy and at least one big-and-tall specialty account, in writing, before the buy - because a full size run that only lives on Nike.com does not deliver the proposition.

The full-price story must survive the most promoted band in the category. Nike's markdown rate and weeks-of-supply for basketball shorts by wholesale partner across a full year (not an August snapshot, when shorts always clear), showing whether a differentiated long short can hold USD 55.
what_we_still_dont_know: Unit share by inseam. The single most important number for this decision and it appears nowhere in seven specialist files, three skeptic rounds or the cross-dataset audit.

How big the coverage-first population actually is. Nobody has sized the taller, longer-legged and modest-dressing player segment in any market. The evidence is three qualitative items, two of them from 2014-2017.

Whether the AND1 buyer is choosing price or choosing inclusion. 'Affordable and cultural' is one anonymous review. If the driver is price, a USD 55 Nike short addresses the wrong motive entirely - the same failure mode the skeptic identified in the Philippines local-identity opportunity.

What Nike's actual extended-size assortment and size-curve fill look like globally. This session confirmed the category pages exist and that Kohl's Big & Tall carries the two cheapest franchises, but not the full SKU-by-size-by-price matrix, and no retail page could be retrieved rather than summarised.

Whether women's basketball shorts demand is player demand or fan and lifestyle demand. Ed Stack's own words describe 'boys and girls, young men and women' buying, Sabrina reviewers report wearing them at home more than playing, and the WNBA merchandise figures underwriting the women's story are a 2024 league release on a pre-Clark base.
The return rate and return-reason mix for Nike basketball shorts, benchmarked against Nike apparel overall. The grading argument in this brief assumes fit returns are elevated and nobody has checked.
Whether a USD 55 long short cannibalises the USD 37 opening 11" or expands the pool. Held-out-market testing would answer it; nothing in this base does.

What the same architecture looks like outside the US. Every price, competitor and channel datapoint underneath this opportunity is American, and the base's own geographic-bias audit flags US over-representation across all seven domains.
nike_right_to_win:
This is one of the few opportunities in the portfolio that Nike is uniquely positioned to execute BECAUSE it already owns the problem.

1. NIKE CREATED THE INVERSION, SO NIKE CAN FIX IT UNILATERALLY. No competitor set has to move. The action is a line-architecture and price-file decision inside a franchise Nike already runs at 6, 8, 10 and 11 inches with pockets at every length, in a size run that already reaches 4XL Tall at Kohl's and 3X on Nike.com. Nothing here requires inventing a category; it requires re-rating one Nike already ships.

2. THE COMPETITORS HOLDING THIS SPACE CANNOT FOLLOW UP-MARKET. AND1 at USD 9.98 to 5XL has no performance credential to charge USD 55 with. Mitchell & Ness owns the length through licensed team IP, which caps it in fan doors and prices it into a clearance cycle from USD 79.99 to USD 35.99 - and licensed heritage cannot make a performance construction claim. Amazon private label competes on pack economics. None of them can make a waistband, grading and wash-durability argument on a performance wall.

3. THE DUTY STACK IS WORKING FOR NIKE HERE, NOT AGAINST IT. The US de minimis repeal and roughly 53.5% apparel duty stack hit the direct-from-China value floor hardest; Temu and Shein US audiences remain about 30% below pre-tariff baseline. Nike is absorbing USD 1.5B of tariff cost too, but it is absorbing it with a sourcing base and scale the USD 9.98 competitor does not have.

4. NIKE HAS THE PATTERN CAPABILITY AND THE PROOF POINT. Sabrina demonstrated that a genuine women's construction - woven front, knit back, plus-size SKU - earns USD 65. Nike's own DNA make (mesh face, smooth knit inner, zip utility pocket sized for a phone) is the right chassis. What has never been done is applying that construction discipline to the long lengths and the extended grades.

5. THE CHANNEL IS ALREADY BUILT AND ALREADY WINNING. Kohl's, Dick's, Academy, Hibbett and Amazon carry Nike basketball shorts in extended sizes today, and Nike wholesale grew 4% in FY26 while Digital fell for a tenth straight quarter. This does not need a new route to market.

6. IT IS THE CHEAPEST BET IN THE PORTFOLIO TO TEST. No new material, no new platform, no athlete dependency, no regional creation centre. The two decisive tests - unit share by inseam, and a price test on a USD 37-to-USD 55 step - are both cheap and both already scoped in the validation list.

Honest limit on the right to win: Nike's credibility with this consumer is currently damaged, not neutral. The Icon franchise draws 'paper-thin', see-through and holes-after-one-wash complaints at 3.9 stars and 67% recommending, and Icon is one of exactly two franchises Nike offers this consumer in Big & Tall. Nike has to earn the trade-up from a position where it is already the disappointing option in that size range.

narrative:
This spec was built backwards from a number that nobody in the base treated as a finding. The datapoint - Nike DNA Academy 11 inches, USD 37, including Big and Tall - appears in this evidence base exactly twice, both times as skeptic counter-evidence deployed to REFUTE something else: once to kill A02's 'contested USD 45-50 core', once to kill A07's 'design at the poles'. It was used as a weapon and then discarded. Plotted against DNA 6 inches at USD 65 and the 10 inch discounting 38%, it is a price line that slopes the wrong way: the more of you the garment covers, and the more sizes it comes in, the less Nike charges for it.

I spent the first pass trying to break that. It survived. I reproduced three anchors independently on 2 September 2026 - the USD 65 six-inch, the USD 37 eleven-inch, and AND1's 11-inch to 5XL at USD 9.98 - and found something stronger than the synthesis had: Kohl's Big and Tall Nike basketball assortment is composed of exactly two franchises, DNA Academy and Icon, which are Nike's two cheapest. That is not an inference about extended sizes being an afterthought. That is the assortment.

The hardest judgement call was what the opportunity actually IS. The synthesis frames it partly as whitespace. It is not whitespace, and I have said so in three places. Nike runs a live Women's Plus Size Basketball Shorts page and a live Men's Big and Tall Basketball Shorts page; Nike already markets an 11-inch for 'extra coverage'; Nike already sells a 9-inch women's short. Every specialist in this base got burned for proposing products Nike ships, and I was not going to make it eight. The honest claim is narrower and, I think, more useful: coverage and extended sizes exist inside Nike, and they exist only as the entry make. That is a repricing and reconstruction move on a live assortment, not an entry into empty space - and it is a claim a PLM can check in an afternoon against the internal price file.

The second argument I had with myself was the inseam war. A07 says design at the poles and abandon the middle. A02's own source says 7-9 inches. Hibbett says retro is 9-plus. Nike ships 6 through 11 continuously. The auditor's verdict is that nobody holds a single unit of sell-through by inseam, and I refuse to launder that into a direction. So Full Range is deliberately NOT a bet that long is winning. It is a bet that whatever share the long end holds, it is currently built and priced as if it were worthless. If unit share by inseam comes back showing the 9-11 band collapsing, the length half of this brief should be cut and the size half kept.

The third call was price, and it is where I am least comfortable. USD 55 puts the tier at the Standard Issue rung, USD 18 above the current 11-inch and USD 10 below the 6-inch, and it holds the USD 37 opening price so the ladder gains a step rather than losing one. It also asks the most price-sensitive buyer in the category for a 49% trade-up, against an AND1 alternative at USD 9.98 that is genuinely inclusive to 5XL and that one reviewer called 'affordable and cultural'. I could not find a single willingness-to-pay datapoint anywhere in seven specialist files. The flat MSRP across extended sizes costs margin points because big sizes eat more fabric; I have kept that cost visible rather than engineering it away, because engineering it away is the exact behaviour this brief exists to correct.

What argues hardest against the whole thing is not a competitor. It is Nike's own review corpus. The Icon franchise - one of the two Nike offers this consumer in Big and Tall - runs 3.9 stars with 67 percent recommending across 64 reviews, and the reproducible complaints are seams failing and shrinkage after one wash. Nike is not neutral with this buyer. It is the disappointing option in that size range, asking for a trade-up. That is why the confidence is 58, why the hangtag carries a wash-durability spec, and why I would not take this past Consumer Council without the two tests attached.
